{{Short description|American mathematician (1871–1959)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=July 2025}}
'''Arnold Frederick Emch''' (24 March 1871 in [[Hessigkofen]], Switzerland<ref name=Marquis>[https://archive.org/details/whoswho141926/page/604/mode/2up EMCH, Arnold], in ''[[Who's Who in America]]'' (14th edition, 1926); p. 663</ref>–1959) was a Swiss-American mathematician, known for his work on the [[inscribed square problem]].

After studying at [[ETH Zurich]] from 1890 to 1893, Emch traveled to America,<ref name=Marquis/> and received his Ph.D. in 1895 at the [[University of Kansas]] under the supervision of Henry Byron Newson.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=5657}}</ref><ref>Henry Byron Newson was the husband of [[Mary Frances Winston Newson]].</ref> In the late 1890s until 1905, he was an assistant professor of graphic mathematics in the school of engineering at the Kansas State Agricultural College (now [[Kansas State University]]).<ref>{{cite book|author=Walters, John Daniel|title=History of the Kansas State Agricultural College|publisher=Printing Department of the Kansas state agricultural college, 1909|year=1909|pages=[https://archive.org/details/historyofkansass00walt/page/123 123]|url=https://archive.org/details/historyofkansass00walt}}</ref> In 1905, Emch became a professor of mathematics at the Kantonsschule in [[Canton of Solothurn|Solothurn, Switzerland]].<ref name="GradMag">{{cite book|chapter=Arnold Emch|title=The Graduate Magazine of the University of Kansas|year=1908|volume=8|page=277|chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=MXzOAAAAMAAJ&pg=PA277}}</ref> In 1908, Emch gave a lecture at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in [[Rome]].<ref name=GradMag/> From 1911 to 1939, he was a professor at the [[University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign]].<ref>[http://archives.library.illinois.edu/archon/?p=collections/controlcard&id=3866 Arnold Emch Papers, 1901–1954; University of Illinois Archives]</ref>

His wife was Hilda Walters Emch and they had two sons, Walter Emch and Arnold Frederick Emch, a well-known management consultant.<ref>Arnold Frederick Emch (1899–1989) was the author of the 1965 book ''Uncommon letters to a son''.</ref>
